determinism.note: llamacpp_adapter passes SETTINGS.llm.seed (42) to the model constructor, so the seed is applied once at load and each later call advances the random state. The repeat run of iteration 3 was byte-identical because both runs were the first call after a backend restart. Every iteration in this comparison was run the same way, so the comparison is controlled; outside that setup identical prompts do not give identical posts.
determinism.correction_2026_09_13: Earlier text said these scores carry no sampling noise in general. That was wrong; it holds only for the first call after a model load.

caveats: n=1 BRIEF. Each post was the first generation after a fresh model load, which is what makes the runs comparable - the seed is applied once at load, not per call. Every number comes from one topic, one audience and one fact set; nothing here shows the fixes generalise.
The two large moves (audience 0.1333->0.7333, factual 0.50->1.00) are driven by deterministic checks that are also covered by 43 unit tests, so they are not artefacts of a single generation.

The small moves are NOT improvements and should not be read as such: style 0.8487->0.8487 and structure 0.8333->0.8333 are unchanged, while technical 0.80->0.7333 and audience's shortfall from 1.0 are real, unaddressed losses in this sample.
content_score is stuck at 0.5 across all four runs - it measures keyword coverage against a 12-term expectation and was not a target of any fix.
Iteration 2 scored WORSE than iteration 1 overall (0.6599 vs 0.6791). It is retained because it made the failure visible and exposed the broken repair path, not because it improved the output.
